summary: Serve current client runtime pages from complete background publications instead of reducing the fleet on each request

replay.detail: Publications are disposable in-memory views rebuilt from existing claims.

schema.detail: No durable schema or claim vocabulary changes.

rules.detail: Runtime authority, current/history classification and resource ordering use the existing status reduction.

compatibility.detail: Current runtime list pages serve the latest complete publication and identify its snapshot and publication time. Before the first publication they return HTTP 503 runtime-list-not-ready; an ended refresher returns runtime-list-ended. Cursor expiry and frozen collection continuations are preserved across republishes. History lists and exact detail reads retain their existing path; terminal capabilities remain caller-scoped.

downtime.detail: No migration; the first publication warms after daemon startup.

manual.detail: OTel exposes st.runtime_list.publication.age as a seconds gauge and st.runtime_list.rebuild.duration as a seconds histogram. The shared collection refresher coalesces commits and limits rebuild concurrency to one. Full collection rebuilding remains background work.

recovery.detail: Restart reconstructs the publication. Binary rollback requires no data changes.
